title: Range-for Copies
explanation:
`for (int x : v)` copies each element into `x`, so `x *= 2` only doubles the copy and the vector doesn't change.

`for (int& x : v)` binds `x` to each element, so `x += 1` really changes the vector: `{2, 3, 4}`.

The same bug is easy to write with big objects too, plus a performance cost: `for (auto s : strings)` copies every string. Use `const auto&` to read and `auto&` to modify.
